vault.title: Lab 01 - Image basics (numpy)
vault.summary: This document outlines the first laboratory assignment for an Introduction to Computer Vision course, focusing on treating images as NumPy arrays. Students are required to build a 64x64 RGB gradient image, convert it to grayscale, perform array slicing and flipping, compute histograms, and apply thresholding. The final deliverable is a Jupyter notebook named lab01.ipynb containing code cells for each of the five tasks.

vault.title: CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision Syllabus
vault.summary: This document outlines the 15-week schedule, grading policy, and lab assignments for CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision taught by Abenova Saule. Students will learn about image processing, feature detection, camera models, and convolutional neural networks. The final grade is determined by labs, a midterm exam, and a final project.
key_terms: Convolution: A mathematical operation used in linear filtering for image processing.
Edge detection: Techniques like Sobel and Canny to identify boundaries within images.
SIFT: Scale-Invariant Feature Transform used for detecting and describing local features.
Homography: A transformation relating the coordinates of points in two images.
RANSAC: An iterative algorithm to estimate mathematical model parameters from noisy data.
Optical flow: The pattern of apparent motion of objects in a visual scene.
YOLO: An object detection system looking at images once to detect objects in real-time.

vault.title: Lecture 01: Introduction
vault.summary: This document introduces CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision taught by Abenova Saule at KBTU. It covers the course overview, grading policy, and the representation of digital images as multi-dimensional arrays. Students are also introduced to essential programming tools like numpy, OpenCV, and matplotlib.
key_terms: Computer Vision: A field of artificial intelligence that enables computers to derive meaningful information from digital images.
Image Arrays: The representation of images as matrices defined by height, width, and color channels.
dtype uint8: An 8-bit unsigned integer data type commonly used to store pixel intensity values ranging from 0 to 255.
numpy: A Python library used for working with large multi-dimensional arrays and matrices.
OpenCV: An open-source computer vision and machine learning software library.
matplotlib: A plotting library for the Python programming language and its numerical mathematics extension NumPy.
